P1:
Jan 14, 2026 Roblox renamed 46 yielding methods with an Async suffix (DevForum PSA). Old names are deprecated "informationally": same behaviour, not scheduled for removal, but Script Analysis flags them, so use new names in new code.
- Player:LoadCharacter -> Player:LoadCharacterAsync (old still works)
- BadgeService:AwardBadge -> BadgeService:AwardBadgeAsync (old still works)
- MarketplaceService:GetProductInfo -> GetProductInfoAsync (old still works; same args/returns)
- Instance:WaitForChild -> NOT renamed; still WaitForChild
- RemoteFunction:InvokeServer -> NOT renamed; still InvokeServer (InvokeClient and BindableFunction:Invoke also unchanged)
Caveat: very old mobile client builds briefly lacked some Async names; irrelevant on the server. (Source: Engine and API Changes 2025-2026.)
P2:
Server Authority (full release July 9, 2026) is opt-in: in Workspace properties, Server Authority section, set AuthorityMode = Server. It forces five settings: NextGenerationReplication = Enabled, PlayerScriptsUseInputActionSystem = Enabled, SignalBehavior = Deferred, StreamingEnabled = Enabled, UseFixedSimulation = Enabled (so you inherit all streaming and deferred-signal bugs).
Predicted gameplay logic goes in a function registered with RunService:BindToSimulation(fn), shared by client and server (e.g. a ModuleScript in ReplicatedStorage required by both). It can be re-run during resimulation, so it must be deterministic: read input from InputAction objects (not UserInputService), keep custom state in attributes on predicted instances (first 64 replicate, names/strings max 50 chars), no Destroy/reparent/EquipTool inside it (record intent, destroy in PostSimulation on server). Clock: use time() (simulation time); not tick(), os.time(), os.clock() or task.wait timing. VFX/sounds go in RenderStepped and must tolerate rollbacks. (Server Authority and Input Migration 2026.)

P5:
Since 2025-26 the binding limits are per experience, not per server. From July 29, 2026 in-game and Open Cloud DataStore requests share one per-experience budget per request type, base raised to 300. Per minute (CCU = concurrent users):
- Read: 300 + 40 x CCU
- Write: 300 + 20 x CCU
- List: 300 + 2 x CCU
- Remove: 300 + 40 x CCU
UpdateAsync costs one read AND one write (counts against both budgets). Per key: value up to 4 MB (4,194,304 chars) and 4 MB/min write throughput. Storage limit: 500 MB + 1 MB per lifetime player (enforced since April 2026). Old per-server limits (60 + 40 x players etc.) still exist but are no longer the binding constraint. Trap: Open Cloud bulk jobs now spend the same budget as live servers; self-throttle with DataStoreService:GetRequestBudgetForRequestType. (Data and Cloud Changes 2025-2026.)

G1:
Rules for MarketplaceService.ProcessReceipt:
1. Exactly one script assigns it (only the last assignment wins).
2. Idempotent per receiptInfo.PurchaseId: record granted PurchaseIds (in the player's save or a purchase-history DataStore) and if already recorded, return PurchaseGranted without granting again.
3. Return PurchaseGranted ONLY after the grant is durably saved (e.g. UpdateAsync committing both the item and the PurchaseId atomically).
4. Return NotProcessedYet on any failure: player not in server, DataStore error, unknown product. Roblox will retry (on rejoin/next purchase).
5. Wrap yields in pcall; never error out of the callback; don't yield forever.
6. Grant on the server only; never trust a client "I bought it" remote.
Charged but nothing: callback returned PurchaseGranted before/despite a failed save, errored, the player left and code returned Granted, or another script overwrote the handler. Received twice: no PurchaseId dedupe, so a retry (after a timeout, NotProcessedYet, or a save that succeeded but the function errored/server crashed before returning) grants again; or granting via PromptProductPurchaseFinished as well.
G2:
Use UpdateAsync whenever the new value depends on the old value or more than one server/process may write the key: incrementing currency, appending inventory, session locking, purchase receipts, teleports/rejoins. SetAsync blindly overwrites, so a stale server (or a GetAsync-then-SetAsync race) rolls back or dupes data. SetAsync is fine only for a brand-new key or data nobody else writes.
Transform function rules:
- Must not yield (no task.wait, no other DataStore calls, no remotes).
- May be called multiple times (on conflict it re-runs with fresher data), so it must be pure/side-effect-free: don't grant items or fire events inside it; do that after UpdateAsync returns successfully.
- Handle nil (new player) old values.
- Return nil to cancel the write (e.g. session locked by another server, or data version newer than expected).
- Return the new value (avoid mutating shared state), plus optional userIds/metadata.
- Keep it fast; serializable values only.
Wrap UpdateAsync in pcall with retries/backoff. It costs one read + one write of budget.
G3:
Not safe. typeof(gold) == "number" accepts NaN and inf. NaN fails every comparison, so `gold < 0` and `gold > player.Gold.Value` are both false and NaN passes; fractions (0.5) and -0 pass too. NaN then poisons balances (NaN arithmetic) and can break/dupe trades. Also no rate limit, and it's time-of-check vs time-of-use: gold isn't reserved, so the player can make several offers or spend the gold before the trade completes.
Fix:
```lua
offerRemote.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, gold)
  if typeof(gold) ~= "number" or gold ~= gold or gold % 1 ~= 0 then return end -- NaN, inf, fractions
  if gold < 1 or gold > 1e9 then return end
  if not rateLimit(player) then return end
  local bal = getServerBalance(player) -- server-side data
  if gold > bal then return end
  createOffer(player, gold) -- escrow/reserve gold now; re-validate balance at trade completion
end)
```
(inf % 1 is NaN, so the integer check also rejects inf.)
G4:
Motor6D.Transform is the animation offset and is owned by the Animator: every frame, during the animation step, the Animator overwrites Transform for every joint a playing track keys. Your idle animation keys the barrel joint, so whatever you wrote in Heartbeat is replaced on the next animation step before it is rendered (or jitters).
Fix: write procedural offsets after animation is applied for the frame and before physics/render: connect to RunService.PreSimulation (formerly Stepped), which runs after the Animator updates Transform, and compose rather than replace: motor.Transform = motor.Transform * aimOffset (keeps idle sway). Or remove the barrel joint's keyframes from the idle animation, or use IKControl.
Edit C0 (or C1) instead when it's a persistent/structural offset that isn't per-frame and should replicate from the server (e.g. a mount offset, or a low-rate server-set aim everyone sees). C0 isn't touched by animations, so animation layers on top; but rewriting C0 every frame is costlier and replicates if done on the server. Do per-frame visual aim on the client.
G5:
Roblox resolves per joint, using AnimationPriority: Core < Idle < Movement < Action < Action2 < Action3 < Action4. For each joint, only tracks at the highest priority that animate that joint contribute; lower-priority tracks are ignored on that joint. The default walk is Movement priority. If your swing was left at Core/Idle (or Movement), the walk wins or blends with it, so the swing looks weak or invisible. Fix: set the swing animation (or track.Priority) to Action or higher and make sure it keys the arm joints.
Weights: when several tracks share the same highest priority on a joint they blend by effective weight (track:AdjustWeight(weight, fadeTime); default 1, ramped by fadeTime in Play). Contributions are normalised by total weight, so two weight-1 tracks give 50/50 - why same-priority conflicts look weak. Weight does not override priority: a weight-1 Action track fully overrides Movement on joints it keys. Joints the higher track doesn't key fall back to lower priorities (so legs still walk).
G6:
Unit mismatch. Blender's default scene is 1 unit = 1 metre with Unit Scale 1.0, and FBX stores centimetres, so the exporter writes your model with a 100x scale factor; Studio reads the FBX units and 1 Blender metre ends up ~100 studs (often combined with unapplied object scale).
Roblox-recommended Blender setup: Scene Properties > Units: Unit Scale 0.01 (so 1 Blender unit maps to 1 stud), set before modelling/rigging; apply transforms (Ctrl+A > All Transforms). FBX export: Limit to Selected Objects, Apply Scalings = FBX Units Scale (or FBX All), Forward -Z, Up Y, Apply Unit on, Apply Transform on, object types Mesh/Armature; rigs: Add Leaf Bones off; Path Mode Copy + Embed Textures for textures.
Check the size in the 3D Importer preview (you can also adjust scale/file units there), or export .glb, which uses metres and imports at sensible size. Don't just shrink rigs in Studio, since animation data stays at the wrong scale.
G7:
The glTF exporter only writes evaluated modifiers when "Apply Modifiers" (Include/Data > Mesh > Apply Modifiers) is enabled; otherwise it exports the base mesh, i.e. the unmirrored half and unbevelled sharp edges. Roblox can't apply Blender modifiers itself.
Fix: tick Apply Modifiers in the glTF export dialog, or apply the modifiers (Ctrl+A) on a copy before export.
Catch: the exporter's Apply Modifiers doesn't work with shape keys - meshes with shape keys (morph targets) either lose the shape keys or skip modifier application, and skinned meshes need the Armature modifier left unapplied/last (applying it bakes the pose). It also raises triangle count (Bevel adds lots of geometry; watch Roblox's per-MeshPart triangle limit, ~20k). For rigged/shape-key meshes, apply Mirror/Bevel manually first, keep Armature last. Also check normals, since edge look depends on exported normals.
G8:
1) Scale sizing: fromScale(0.3,0.3) is 30% of width and 30% of height of the viewport. Screens have different aspect ratios (16:9 monitor, ~19.5:9 phone, 4:3 tablet), so the frame's pixel aspect changes and it stretches/squashes. Fix: add a UIAspectRatioConstraint (AspectRatio = desired w/h, e.g. 1 for square; DominantAxis) to the frame, or SizeConstraint = RelativeYY/RelativeXX, plus UISizeConstraint for min/max pixels; UIScale for global scaling; AnchorPoint so it scales from the right corner.
2) Notch/top bar: the ScreenGui draws into the unsafe area (IgnoreGuiInset = true and/or ScreenInsets = None). Fix: ScreenGui.ScreenInsets = Enum.ScreenInsets.CoreUISafeInsets (avoids Roblox top-bar buttons plus notch/rounded corners), IgnoreGuiInset = false; DeviceSafeInsets if you only need to avoid the notch. Put only decorative full-bleed backgrounds in a separate ScreenGui with ScreenInsets = None. Add small UIPadding and test with Studio's device emulator (notched phone).

```lua
-- Server Script
local RS = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local Items = require(game.ServerScriptService.ItemCatalog) -- server-trusted {[id]={price=number,maxQty=number}}
local Data = require(game.ServerScriptService.PlayerData) -- server-owned profiles
local remote = RS.Remotes.BuyItem
local last = {}

remote.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, itemId, quantity)
	local now = os.clock()
	if last[player] and now - last[player] < 0.25 then return end -- rate limit
	last[player] = now
	if typeof(itemId) ~= "string" or #itemId > 64 then return end
	if typeof(quantity) ~= "number" or quantity ~= quantity or quantity % 1 ~= 0 then return end -- NaN/inf/fractions
	local item = Items[itemId]
	if not item then return end
	if quantity < 1 or quantity > (item.maxQty or 99) then return end
	local profile = Data.get(player)
	if not profile then return end -- not loaded yet
	local cost = item.price * quantity -- price from server, never client
	if profile.Coins < cost then return end
	profile.Coins -= cost
	profile.Inventory[itemId] = (profile.Inventory[itemId] or 0) + quantity
	Data.markDirty(player) -- saved via UpdateAsync + session lock
end)
Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(p) last[p] = nil end)
```
Server owns price, balance and inventory; validate every arg; check and spend in one block with no yields between.

```lua
-- Key "u_<userId>" value: {data=..., lock={jobId=, time=}}
local LOCK_TTL = 1800 -- stale lock expiry (s), for crashed servers
local function load(player)
  for attempt = 1, 5 do
    local ok, result = pcall(store.UpdateAsync, store, key(player), function(old)
      old = old or {data = defaultData(), lock = nil}
      local l = old.lock
      if l and l.jobId ~= game.JobId and os.time() - l.time < LOCK_TTL then
        return nil -- locked by another server: cancel write
      end
      old.lock = {jobId = game.JobId, time = os.time()}
      return old
    end)
    if ok and result and result.lock and result.lock.jobId == game.JobId then return result.data end
    task.wait(attempt * 2) -- other server may still be releasing (teleport/rejoin)
  end
  player:Kick("Data busy, please rejoin") -- never play on default data
end
local function save(player, release)
  store:UpdateAsync(key(player), function(old)
    if not old or not old.lock or old.lock.jobId ~= game.JobId then return nil end -- lost lock: don't overwrite
    old.data = sessions[player].data
    old.lock = if release then nil else {jobId = game.JobId, time = os.time()}
    return old
  end)
end
```
Plus: autosave every 60-120s (refreshes lock), save+release on PlayerRemoving and BindToClose (wait for all), save+release before TeleportAsync, pcall + retries, block trades/purchases until loaded, receipts (PurchaseIds) in the same document. ProfileStore implements this pattern.

T4:
FireServer automatically passes the calling player as the first argument on the server. The client also passed LocalPlayer explicitly, so the server receives (player, LocalPlayer, 50): `amount` is the Player instance and 50 is a third, ignored argument, hence arithmetic on an Instance.
Fix the client: `remote:FireServer(50)`. Server keeps `function(player, amount)`, and validate since clients can send anything:
```lua
remote.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, amount)
  if typeof(amount) ~= "number" or amount ~= amount then return end
  print(amount + 1)
end)
```
Never trust a player argument sent by the client; use the implicit first parameter.
T5:
Race condition: in Studio solo play the local player can join before the server Script runs and connects Players.PlayerAdded (especially if the script yields or requires modules first), so PlayerAdded never fires for that player. Live servers usually start before anyone joins.
Standard fix: connect, then handle players already present:
```lua
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local function onPlayerAdded(player)
  local ls = Instance.new("Folder"); ls.Name = "leaderstats"
  local coins = Instance.new("IntValue"); coins.Name = "Coins"; coins.Parent = ls
  ls.Parent = player
end
Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(onPlayerAdded)
for _, p in Players:GetPlayers() do task.spawn(onPlayerAdded, p) end
```
Connect before any yields (WaitForChild, slow requires, DataStore calls) and make the handler safe to run once per player.

T8:
Likely mesh streaming + cloud LoDs. Since April 2026 Workspace.MeshStreamingAndImprovedLoDs (Default/Enabled/Disabled) exists; when Enabled, every mesh uses the cloud LoD transcoder and mesh streaming and MeshPart.RenderFidelity is ignored, so meshes drop detail with distance/memory regardless of Precise. Phase 2 (planned ~July 2026) makes Default map to Enabled (unverified whether shipped); Phase 3 removes RenderFidelity.
What to do: check the property's effective value in Studio; Disabled is at most a temporary escape (removal path). The real fix is budgeting triangles at the source (clean topology, silhouette-preserving geometry) and not relying on RenderFidelity. Also: RenderFidelity can't be changed by scripts at runtime (set it in Studio before publishing), Studio can show a different LoD than live, and there are reported bugs of meshes stuck at lowest LoD (report with repro). Collision geometry is unaffected. (Engine and API Changes 2025-2026.)
